findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently removes the (width, height) variant
findings.body: `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). Ruby has no method overloading, so only the 3/4-argument version survives and any existing caller that passes `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (4 positional args + opts) now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`. Either keep one signature or give the dimension-string variant a different name (e.g. `downsize_to`).

findings.title: Removal of `self.dimensions` and change of `optimize` signature breaks external callers
findings.body: `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted and `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`. These are public class methods used by plugins/specs and other call sites; existing calls will now raise `NoMethodError` / `ArgumentError`. If the change is intended, the old entry points should be kept as deprecated shims or all call sites and specs updated in the same PR.

findings.title: Animated-GIF downsize path passes a percentage to gifsicle, which it does not accept
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` ends up in `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects explicit `WxH` dimensions (percentages are only supported by `--scale`), so the command fails, `convert_with` returns false, and the while loop spins through all 5 attempts without shrinking the file. Large animated GIFs will then be rejected by the size validation even though the feature claims to downsize them.

findings.title: In-place downsize can leave a stale file handle, causing a wrong filesize and corrupt upload
findings.body: The loop runs `convert` with the same path as both source and destination and then re-reads `tempfile.size` / passes `tempfile` to `Upload.create_for`. ImageMagick may replace the file (new inode) rather than truncate it, in which case the still-open Tempfile descriptor refers to the old, unlinked inode: `tempfile.size` keeps reporting the pre-resize size (loop burns all 5 attempts) and `Upload.create_for` stores the original, un-resized bytes. The tempfile is also never rewound after the external process writes to it. Reopen/stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`) and rewind/reopen the handle before creating the upload, or write to a fresh temp file.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a hardcoded constant. Admins who lowered the limit can no longer restrict API URL uploads, and admins who raised it above 10MB will have downloads truncated/rejected. The cap should be derived from the relevant site setting (and from the attachment limit when the upload is not an image, since this path handles both).

findings.title: Client-side size check hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
findings.body: `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Non-image attachments are not auto-downsized by the new server code, so an attachment between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10MB now passes client validation and is only rejected by the server, producing a confusing late failure. Conversely, sites configured with a limit above 10MB will have valid uploads blocked in the browser. The limit should stay driven by the per-type site setting (images can be allowed to exceed it since they get downsized).

findings.title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit that may not match the server
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. A 413 usually comes from the web server's own body-size limit, so the user is shown a number unrelated to the actual limit, which is misleading when the site is configured differently.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path
findings.body: The new downsize loop in `create_upload` (retry count, interaction with `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, animated GIF handling, images that still exceed the limit after 5 attempts) and the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures are not covered by any test in this PR, so the duplicate-method and gifsicle problems went unnoticed. Add controller/model specs covering an oversized image upload and a still-too-large image.
